title: VeriContest: A Competitive-Programming Benchmark for Verifiable Code Generation
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: A single worked example shows that verifiable code generation requires producing specification, code, and proof together, not code alone.
layout: 2 side-by-side code panels, left-to-right, color-highlighted line-numbered code
description: Two side-by-side code listings with line numbers, taken from a Verus/Rust solution to LeetCode 34 (search range in a sorted array). The left panel shows the function signature in light blue (code), followed by a large orange block holding the requires/ensures clauses (specification), then an elided comment and the opening brace. The right panel continues the same function. It shows a light-blue while-loop header, a lavender invariant and decreases block (proof), and light-blue binary-search body lines. Elision comments mark omitted parts, such as the remaining postconditions and the second binary search. The three background colors (orange, blue, purple) separate the three artifacts. The eye goes first to the large orange specification block, then across to the purple proof annotations interleaved with the code.
caption: An example Verus problem illustrating the three artifacts of verifiable code generation: \highlight{Orange!25}{specification}, \highlight{SkyBlue!25}{code}, and \highlight{Purple!15}{proofs}. This example (LeetCode 34) returns the first and last indices of the target value (\CodeIn{target}) in a sorted array via two binary searches.
abstract: Large language models can generate useful code from natural language, but their outputs come without correctness guarantees. Verifiable code generation offers a path beyond testing by requiring models to produce not only executable code, but also formal specifications and machine-checkable proofs. Progress in this direction, however, is difficult to measure: existing benchmarks are often small, cover only part of the pipeline, lack ground-truth proofs or rigorous specification validation, or target verification settings far from mainstream software development. We present VeriContest, a benchmark of 1,006 competitive-programming problems from LeetCode and Codeforces for verifiable code generation in Rust with Verus. Each problem includes a natural language description, expert-validated formal specifications, judge-accepted Rust code, Verus-checked proofs, and positive and negative test suites. VeriContest is constructed through a three-phase pipeline that scales from manually verified seed problems to semi-automated expansion with human-in-the-loop review. To strengthen benchmark quality, we also use testing to validate postcondition completeness. VeriContest supports both isolated and compositional evaluation of specification, code, and proof generation, and end-to-end verified program synthesis. Evaluating ten state-of-the-art models reveals a sharp gap between ordinary coding and verifiable code generation: the strongest model reaches 97.51% on natural-language-to-code generation, but only 57.16% on specification generation, 13.82% on proof generation, and 6.76% end-to-end. These results identify proof and specification generation as the central bottlenecks for current models and establish VeriContest as a rigorous platform for evaluating and training future systems that generate code with machine-checkable correctness.
